record_reviews.summary: Blyth’s notes use W. Allen’s Niger narrative to extract questions about African fowls, Hausa sheep, ducks, cattle and turkeys; compare the fallow deer and stag horn diagram; describe Indian donkeys and zebra striping; revisit double-spurred Gallinaceous birds; distinguish chaus-like domestic cats from F. viverrinus; propose a history of cultivated roses and ancient gardening; and add notes on the Mauritius snail and Kentucky cave animals. The body moves from cited travel observations to Blyth’s own field observations and speculative questions.
record_reviews.date_assessment: [22 October 1855] is the XML single day (1855-10-22), but the brackets signal editorial dating; dispatch and Darwin receipt are not shown. It is headed “Notes for Mr Darwin”, not a conventional letter.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Blyth voice; Allen, Fraser, Gosse, Falconer and other authorities are reported sources. The horn drawing is Blyth’s diagram reference, while later CD apparatus remains separate.

alternative_candidates_considered.assessment: Earlier/larger Lyell memorandum contains related geographic and animal questions but is separately dated and not a prompt endpoint.
Cover/enclosure letter establishes transmission of manuscripts, not a Darwin question.
